topics.label: Introduction to cancer evolution and the lecture’s focus
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the class, frames the lecture’s themes, and states its learning aims before the substantive material begins.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and clonal selection in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can give clones a selective advantage and how that selection contributes to cancer evolution.

topics.label: Epigenetic disruption in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic shows how changes in transcriptional availability can contribute to tumor development even without new mutations.

topics.label: Cancer stemness and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine whether cancer growth follows a stem-cell-like hierarchy and how the originating cell type shapes tumor development.

topics.label: Inflammatory microenvironments promoting cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammation can provide conditions that let mutation-bearing cells acquire stem-like properties and form tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cells in an established tumor’s microenvironment can support its growth and offer targets for therapy.

topics.label: Single-cell and spatial methods for studying cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes sequencing and spatial profiling approaches for investigating tumor cells and their interactions.

topics.label: Lecture summary and transition to cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics close the lecture by recapping its main ideas and noting the subject of the next lecture.
